item.title: Martial Arts return to Kavieng

item.content:encoded:
Taekwondo and Karate athletes across New Ireland Province converged in Kavieng yesterday afternoon as the Sir Julius Chan Bismarck Mixed Martial Arts Cup makes its comeback with the completion of day-one of the three-day championships at the Catholic Conference Centre.

The tournament has brought together twelve martial arts clubs from across the province, giving male and female competitors an opportunity to test their skills, demonstrate discipline and compete for honours in the two codes.

Tournament Director, Severious Neki, says the cup tournament returns after a 10-year hiatus, thanks to the support of Governor Byron Chan and the New Ireland Provincial Administration.

Neki says the tournament forms the basis of a talent identification program where the best will be picked to form a provincial team to take part in the Karate Nationals in Lae next month (November) and the Taekwondo Korean Ambassadors' Cup in Port Moresby.

"We are honoured to have chief instructors from PNG Karate Federation in the likes of Vice President Sensei Roy Stanley, Sensei Abel Mekere and team from Port Moresby along with fellow Taekwondo professionals here with us.

"Martial arts isn't just a sport of defence and combat. Martial arts resonate mental control, self-discipline, respect and humility - values we want to encourage among the youth of today," Neki said.

The championships began with the grading category for both codes before going into the Karate Kata tournament in a show of pattern and sequence.

New Ireland Governor Byron Chan took time to be part of the program - he himself a sensei with affiliation and representation for international martial arts organisations around the world. Governor Chan said taekwondo and karate are more than just martial arts.

"They are disciplines that build character, instill respect, promote self-control and develop confidence among our young people. These values are important to New Ireland’s development aspirations because our future depends not only on economic growth and infrastructure, but also on raising a generation of disciplined, responsible and healthy citizens who can contribute positively to their communities.

“The New Ireland Provincial Government supports the revival of the Sir Julius Chan Bismarck Mixed Martial Arts Cup because we recognise the role sport plays in youth development, community engagement and the preservation of positive values. By investing in coaching, strengthening local clubs and creating opportunities for our athletes to compete, we are helping our young people discover their potential and develop skills that will serve them both inside and outside the sporting arena," the Governor said.

He said the Chan-Kolivos Government's vision is to see Taekwondo and Karate grow across the province, with stronger clubs, qualified instructors and a clear pathway for local athletes to compete at national and international levels, including the Pacific Games.

He said, “This is consistent with our broader development aspirations for a stronger, healthier and more empowered New Ireland, where young people are given opportunities to participate, develop their talents and play a meaningful role in building the future of our province.”

Meanwhile, the three-day tournament will feature Karate kata - patterns, Karate kumite - fighting, Taekwondo poomsae - patterns, and finishing off Monday with Taekwondo kyrugi - fighting.

Tournament instructors and rising martial artists, Steven Tommy from New Ireland and Vespa John of Kairuku, had been with the clubs last week, preparing for the tournament, running drills and coaching sessions.

John commended the Governor's support of martial arts, and the time taken to be part of the martial arts community in reviving what once was an annual cup tournament in Kavieng.

item.title: Kundiawa-Gembogl ballot boxes verified and await funding for recount
item.description: The PNG Electoral Commission has confirmed it can now comply with the National Court order for a recount of the Kundiawa-Gembogl Open electorate in Simbu, following a successful verification of ballot boxes in Kundiawa today. The verification exercise was conducted at the Kundiawa Police Station in a transparent manner, witnessed by key stakeholders and members of the public.
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Electoral Commission has confirmed it can now comply with the National Court order for a recount of the Kundiawa-Gembogl Open electorate in Simbu, following a successful verification of ballot boxes in Kundiawa today.

The verification exercise was conducted at the Kundiawa Police Station in a transparent manner, witnessed by key stakeholders and members of the public.

PNG Electoral Commissioner Dr. Nicole Haley said the inspection was witnessed by legal counsels for both the applicant and the respondent, two witnesses nominated by each party, a delegate registrar from Goroka, the Kundiawa Police Station Commander, and police personnel from Kundiawa and Goroka.

She said the primary purpose of the exercise was to ascertain and identify the ballot boxes from the 2021-2022 National General Election.

"We have now confirmed the ballot boxes are intact, so the court order can be complied with," Dr. Haley said.

She stressed that transparency would be maintained throughout the recount process.

"According to the court order, the recount must be conducted in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province. The decision was made to diffuse political tensions in Kundiawa and ensure the recount proceeds peacefully," she said.

She said the container holding the ballot boxes will now be transported from Kundiawa to Goroka under police escort.

She said they are now work on logistics and costing and will seek funding to facilitate the transfer and conduct of the recount.

The court-ordered recount for Kundiawa-Gembogl follows a lengthy election petition challenging the 2022 National General Election result.

item.title: More than a hundred receive King’s Golden Jubilee Medal
item.description: More than a hundred recipients of the Kings Golden Jubilee Medal at the 2026 Central Province Investiture Ceremony received medals and Certificates by His Excellency Grand Chief Sir Bob Dadae, Governor General of Papua New Guinea on Friday. The Kings Golden Jubilee Medal is awarded to individuals for their outstanding and Distinguished service to Papua New Guinea and Central Province. The Ceremony
item.content:encoded:
More than a hundred recipients of the Kings Golden Jubilee Medal at the 2026 Central Province Investiture Ceremony received medals and Certificates by His Excellency Grand Chief Sir Bob Dadae, Governor General of Papua New Guinea on Friday.

The Kings Golden Jubilee Medal is awarded to individuals for their outstanding and Distinguished service to Papua New Guinea and Central Province. The Ceremony at Bautama in Central Province saw 108 recipients awarded with their medals and certificates by his excellency grand chief Sir Bob Dadae and witnessed by their families, friends and colleagues.

Bill Toraso, Official Secretary congratulated the 2026 recipients and thanked them for their service.

“There are three different medals which are presented by his excellency through the same process, the one you are about to receive now is the 50 th Independence Anniversary Kings Golden Jubilee Medal.

“Gold medals that the Governor General presents are blessed by Buckingham palace, and they all recognize the individual contributions by the men and women of our country to develop the country." Toraso said.

Two serving staff of the National Broadcasting Corporation were also part of the cohort; Ms. Rachal Boga Director Provincial Radio at Radio Central and Mr. Wari Ila from the National Newsroom also received their medals for their services to Central and towards nation building in Papua New Guinea.

Acting Provincial Administrator, Magini Raga acknowledged the presence of his excellency and the recipients and apologized for the absence of Madam Governor and the District Members of the Province who had to attend the Parliament sitting.

“Our Nation's Golden Jubilee in 2025 celebrated 50 years of Papua New Guinea's sovereignty, resilience and growth. To my fellow recipients, congratulations and may this recognition inspire to continue serving our people with pride and dedication. May God bless our awardees.” Raga said.

item.title: ESPHA to improve after WHO visit
item.description: East Sepik Provincial Health Authority (ESPHA) sees room for improvement after a joint learning visit aimed at understanding challenges faced by rural facilities and how to help improve Public Health. From Tuesday 13th to Thursday 15th, the East Sepik Provincial Health Authority facilitated a 3-day joint partnership visit with a high-level delegation led by WHO Representative to Papua New Guinea D
item.content:encoded:
East Sepik Provincial Health Authority (ESPHA) sees room for improvement after a joint learning visit aimed at understanding challenges faced by rural facilities and how to help improve Public Health.

From Tuesday 13th to Thursday 15th, the East Sepik Provincial Health Authority facilitated a 3-day joint partnership visit with a high-level delegation led by WHO Representative to Papua New Guinea Dr Rajendra Prasad Yadav, with officials from NDoH, UNICEF, UNAIDS, PATH and DFAT.

The team visited Level 4 Maprik District Hospital, Maprik Secondary School, Level 2 Naramko Health Centre and Kombikum 2 village on Tuesday 13th, and Huliwa Aid Post, Sassoya Level 3 Health Centre, Tumarau Level 3 Sub Health Centre and Passam Aid Post over the next two days.

During a debrief at Village Inn Hotel in Wewak, Manager for the Expanded Program on Immunization at the National Department of Health Martha Pogo called on the Provincial Health Authority to improve monitoring. " Management here when you make budget, allocate some funds for monitoring at least for a quarter or month to visit the lower-level facilities" Pogo said.

She said the team found gaps that need ongoing monitoring. "For Immunization, the SOP's, the guidelines, the registers, the Immunization supply chain standards all updated and sent outside circular after Circular, and it is sad that our facilities are practicing the Old outdated" Pogo said.

ESPHA Chief Executive Officer Mathew Kaluvia thanked the WHO-led team for the learning visit and acknowledged the gaps identified. "It used to be quarterly basis that we started routine Immunization and we made that resolution in 2024" Kaluvia said. " Sight visit, supervision, monitoring and on-sight training must be on monthly basis and East Sepik is going to do that " he said.

" I would want this team to come back again same time next year to go back and visit those areas again" Kaluvia said. " I can assure you that we will improve" he added.

Board Chairman Pastor Max Manimbi said such visits are vital for accountability. "When you operate in a place for a long time, you'll have blinds spots" Manimbi said. "You'll keep seeing the same thing and you'll think it is normal" he said. "It takes another pair of eyes to come and open a new perspective, monitoring and Management is very vital" Manimbi said. He concluded by saying, "The more you come, we keep it real and it's good for us".

item.title: Eight families homeless after bushfire in Chuave
item.description: Eight families have been left homeless after a devastating bushfire swept through Gorokabu community in Chuave District of Simbu Province on Saturday. The fire, fueled by prolonged dry conditions linked to El Niño and strong winds, destroyed eight houses and properties worth over K20,000.
item.content:encoded:
Eight families have been left homeless after a devastating bushfire swept through Gorokabu community in Chuave District of Simbu Province on Saturday.

The fire, fueled by prolonged dry conditions linked to El Niño and strong winds, destroyed eight houses and properties worth over K20,000.

Village Elder, Kaupa Kay, told NBC News the fire broke out in the nearby bush in the afternoon and spread rapidly before residents could contain it.

In addition to the eight houses, three live pigs, five coffee plots and several red pandanus trees - a critical food and cash crop for the community - were completely destroyed.

"No lives were lost; however, families lost all their belongings including bedding, kitchen utensils, school uniforms and stored food", he said.

Allan Yogori, a victim, said, affected families are now sheltering with relatives and sleeping in temporary bush-material huts.

“We have lost everything. Houses, food, coffee gardens that support our children’s school fees are all gone. We are appealing to the Simbu Provincial Disaster Office, the Chuave District Development Authority and the National Government to come and assist our people,” Mr. Yogori said.

He said the community remains highly vulnerable as the dry season continues, with water sources drying up and the risk of further fires increasing.

“This is an El Niño period. We need immediate relief — tarpaulins, food, water containers and building materials. We also ask the Provincial Government to send officers to assess the damage,” he added.

Meanwhile, authorities are urging communities throughout Simbu and the Highlands to take extra precautions during this dry season, as strong winds and dry vegetation have significantly increased the risk of bushfires.

item.title: Haze smoke experienced in Port Moresby
item.description: Hazy smoke has been evident in the skies of Port Moresby for past days. The National Weather Service has explained that the smoky appearance maybe caused by smoke, airborne particles or weather conditions, which are slow in dispersing.
item.content:encoded:
Hazy smoke has been evident in the skies of Port Moresby for past days.

The National Weather Service has explained that the smoky appearance maybe caused by smoke, airborne particles or weather conditions, which are slow in dispersing.

At this time of the year, the Weather Service also noted that Port Moresby is usually affected by dry southeasterly winds which can limit the amount of moisture available for rainfall.

The National Weather Service is yet to confirm the exact cause of the haze smoke being experienced in Port Moresby.

It indicated that the smoky appearance maybe caused by smoke, airborne particles or weather conditions, which are slow in dispersing.

The office noted that haze is heavy during the morning hours when very small particles float in the air and make it difficult to see clearly over long distances.

And, this comes especially from burning grass, bushfires, rubbish, dust from roads among others.

Haze can be harmful to people’s health and therefore the weather office is encouraging people to take precautionary measures like wearing face masks or stay indoors.

Meantime, in a separate report to the National Newspaper, the Weather Service Assistant Director Kasis Inape says the hazy conditions could be associated with fires from Indonesia however further analysis of satellite imagery, fire locations and prevailing wind patterns is required to establish its actual origin.

item.title: Bush fire threatens Lou Island villages in Manus
item.description: A bushfire that has been burning for more than a week on Lou Island in Manus Province is threatening nearby villages, a health centre and food gardens, prompting an urgent appeal for firefighting assistance. According to information provided by local residents, many food gardens have been affected by the blaze, raising concerns about livelihoods and food security.
item.content:encoded:
A bushfire that has been burning for more than a week on Lou Island in Manus Province is threatening nearby villages, a health centre and food gardens, prompting an urgent appeal for firefighting assistance.

According to information provided by local residents, many food gardens have been affected by the blaze, raising concerns about livelihoods and food security.

The situation comes amid the current El Niño period in Papua New Guinea, with dry conditions already affecting food gardens and water supplies on Lou Island. The ongoing bushfire has placed additional pressure on local food production, raising concerns about food security and the livelihoods of households that depend on locally grown produce for their daily needs.

The fire is reportedly close to Lako Village and the health centre, which also serves as the LLG administrative centre. Rei Village is also reported to be in the path of the advancing fire.

The cause of the fire remains unknown. Reports of possible injuries among people involved in firefighting efforts have not been confirmed, while the full extent of the damage is yet to be established.

Local authorities and the Provincial Disaster Office have reportedly been informed of the situation.

The affected community is appealing for urgent assistance, including firefighting personnel, high-volume water pumps and technical support to assess the fire’s boundaries and establish containment lines.

The community is also requesting helicopter support equipped with a monsoon bucket system to deliver water directly onto active sections of the fire and help contain its spread.

Efforts have reportedly been made to seek assistance from Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), the Australian Defence Force and Pacific Helicopters.

The community is urging relevant authorities to coordinate an urgent response to limit further damage and protect nearby villages, food gardens and essential facilities.

The situation remains concerning as residents await further assistance.

item.title: Maprik MP Libert Kapris passes on
item.description: The death of Maprik MP Libert Kapris has been confirmed, sending shockwaves through East Sepik Province and the wider Sepik region. East Sepik Governor Allan Bird confirmed the tragic news in a media statement, saying he had received confirmation from the Deputy Clerk of Parliament.
item.content:encoded:
The death of Maprik MP Libert Kapris has been confirmed, sending shockwaves through East Sepik Province and the wider Sepik region.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird confirmed the tragic news in a media statement, saying he had received confirmation from the Deputy Clerk of Parliament.

Kapris died this morning at PIH in Port Moresby with the cause of death yet to be established, and no further details surrounding the circumstances of his death have been officially released.

Governor Bird described the news as tragic and deeply saddening, saying the Kapris family had suffered significant loss in a short period.

He appealed to the people of Maprik to remain calm during the period of mourning and allow the appropriate arrangements involving Parliament and the family to proceed.

The East Sepik Provincial Government will work closely with the Kapris family and Parliament as funeral arrangements are prepared.

Governor Bird also extended condolences on behalf of the people of the Greater Sepik Region to the Kapris family and their relatives.

Kapris won the Maprik Open by-election in June 2024, representing the People’s First Party, succeeding his father late Gabriel Kapris as Maprik MP.

Further official information regarding the circumstances of his death and funeral arrangements is expected to be released later.
